chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about breast-feeding.
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which is prohibited due to lineage is also prohibited due to breast-feeding.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal equivalence between breast-feeding and blood lineage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the legal effects of breast-feeding (radāʿ) mirror those of blood lineage (nasab), establishing nursing kin as equivalent to consanguineous relatives for marriage prohibitions. This principle, foundational in Shia fiqh, underscores the spiritual and social weight of the nursing bond, ensuring that the same degrees of closeness that preclude marriage between blood relatives also apply to those connected through wet-nursing.
